app_description: This application lets you easily explore the solar potential of a building's roofs and facades. In a few clicks, you can identify the surfaces suitable for a solar installation and discover their potential for electricity or heat production. To learn more about solar installations and the options for your building, find out how to do it in 7 steps ↗.
faq_a1:
The displayed data is based on swisstopo's 3D building model, updated from aerial photographs. Updates to this dataset are carried out progressively across the territory on a 6-year cycle. For this reason, recently built, renovated or converted buildings may not yet appear on the map or may appear with their former geometry.

You can check the update status of your region ↗.
faq_q2: How is the solar potential calculated?
faq_a2:
Roof and facade data comes from swisstopo's 3D model swissBUILDINGS3D and is combined with solar irradiation data from MeteoSwiss ↗ as well as calculation models and simulations developed by Meteotest AG ↗ on behalf of the Swiss Federal Office of Energy (SFOE).

This data enables an estimation of solar potential based on roof geometry, orientation, inclination and solar irradiation received throughout the year. The calculation accounts for shadows cast by terrain, neighboring buildings and vegetation.

For more information on the calculation methodology and data, see the technical documentation ↗.
faq_q3: What is the difference between photovoltaics and solar thermal?
faq_a3:
Photovoltaics (PV) converts solar radiation into electricity. This electricity can be consumed directly in the building, stored or fed into the grid. The estimated PV production depends mainly on available surface area, solar irradiation and panel efficiency.

Solar thermal uses solar energy to produce heat, mainly for domestic hot water or space heating. For the solar thermal estimate, the calculation is based on the estimated heat demand of the building.

The coverage rate shown corresponds to the solar thermal production divided by the building's heat demand (heating + hot water). A value above 100% indicates potential production exceeding the building's needs.

Learn more in the solar installation guide (EnergieSchweiz) ↗. Are you a tenant? Several options are available to you ↗.
faq_a4:
The displayed results are estimates calculated using a large-scale model for all Swiss buildings. The data provides a good indication of a roof's solar potential but does not replace a professional's detailed analysis. Actual production may vary depending on the presence of windows, chimneys, actual roof geometry, immediate surroundings or equipment choices.

Note also that some solar installations remain subject to permits, particularly on protected buildings or in sensitive areas under Art. 18a SPA ↗.
faq_q5: How is the financial return estimated?
faq_a5:
The financial estimate corresponds to the feed-in tariff for energy injected into the grid by a photovoltaic installation with a connection capacity of 10 kVA. This reference tariff is fixed and does not reflect local conditions of your municipality or electricity provider.

The displayed return is an indicative order of magnitude that may change depending on current tariffs, your self-consumption ↗ or electricity buyback conditions.

The feed-in tariff (VESE) shown corresponds to the weighted annual average tariff for a residential PV installation. It includes the remuneration for energy and for the guarantee of origin (GO). Data sourced from pvtarif.ch ↗.
faq_q7: Why is no address displayed for my building?
faq_a7: The displayed addresses come from the Federal Register of Buildings and Dwellings (GWR). This register does not cover all structures: annexes, agricultural buildings, garages or uninhabited constructions are often not listed. In such cases, the solar potential is displayed but without an associated address.
faq_a8:
Data: The data is published as Open Government Data (OGD) and can be freely reused, including for commercial purposes, provided the data source is credited (author, title and link to the dataset).

Download: opendata.swiss ↗ · geocat.ch ↗

Visualization: The data can also be viewed on map.geo.admin.ch ↗, where each individual roof and facade surface can be visualized separately.

Source code: The code of this application is available under the MIT license and can be freely reused. The repository is accessible on GitHub ↗.
faq_q9: The building geometry seems incorrect – why?
faq_a9:
The estimates are based on a large-scale 3D model covering all of Switzerland. For complex roof geometries (multi-pitched roofs, dormers, irregular shapes), discrepancies between the model and reality are possible. These inaccuracies may affect the solar production estimates.

If your building's geometry appears incorrect, we recommend using the EnergieSchweiz solar calculator ↗ for a manual estimate tailored to your situation.
